Website redesign + commerce implementation plan

Izelena Foods
Blueprint & Prototype

A detailed, build-ready plan for a modern Jamaican food brand website, including a complete information architecture, storefront strategy, payment recommendations, responsive design system, content model, acceptance criteria and an interactive visual prototype.

Primary platform: WooCommercePayments: Powertranz + PayPalCurrency: JMD firstPrepared for GPT-5.6 Luna
01 / Executive recommendation

Build a brand-led store, not just a prettier brochure site.

The redesign should preserve the existing family story and recognizable assets while making the products, flavours and purchase path the centre of the experience. The recommended production route is a custom WordPress block theme on WooCommerce, with Powertranz as the primary Caribbean card gateway and PayPal as an additional wallet/payment method.

Why WooCommerce

It provides product variations, inventory, orders, coupons, shipping, tax settings, transactional emails and a client-friendly admin without rebuilding commerce fundamentals from scratch.

Why Powertranz + PayPal

Powertranz is the current brand for First Atlantic Commerce/FAC and is built for Caribbean acquiring relationships. PayPal supports Jamaican business payment use. Both have practical WooCommerce integration routes.

Why not Stripe first

Stripe's merchant payment acceptance list does not currently include Jamaica. Keep a gateway abstraction in the plan, but do not promise Stripe unless the client has a legally eligible merchant account in a supported jurisdiction.

Design deliverable included: the interactive browser prototype below is the immediate design platform for approval. It can be used directly by the implementation agent and later recreated in Figma if a native collaborative design file is required.
02 / Current website audit

What exists today, and what should change.

Retain and strengthen

  • The Miss Izelena origin story in Aboukir, St. Ann.
  • The mother-daughter/family-owned identity and Scotch Bonnet roots.
  • “Exotic Island Flavours for Every Season” and the Jamaican flavour language.
  • The red, yellow, green, black and white brand palette.
  • Existing product photography, face illustration, flower mark, logo and tile pattern.
  • Current address, phone numbers, email and social links after final verification.

Fix or replace

  • The current site has no cart, checkout, pricing, variants or order workflow.
  • Product discovery is shallow; the Sauces page mainly exposes descriptions and images rather than complete commerce-ready product records.
  • The homepage mixes brand story and a form without a strong product-led conversion path.
  • The contact CAPTCHA currently exposes non-English helper text, creating an inconsistent experience.
  • There is no clear retail-versus-wholesale path despite bulk sizes and minimum order quantities in the catalogue.
  • Policies required for e-commerce - shipping, returns, privacy, terms and fulfilment expectations - are incomplete or absent from the primary journey.

03 / Brand and design system

Creative direction: “Modern Jamaican Pantry.”

The visual design should feel handcrafted, warm and proudly Jamaican without becoming visually noisy. Use cream and white as the main canvas, black for structure, and the bright brand colours as purposeful accents. Wood and food photography provide warmth; the tile pattern adds character at low opacity.

Typography

Headings: bold geometric sans, tight tracking and large scale.
Body: neutral sans-serif with generous line height.
Brand script: only through the supplied logo, never imitated in body copy.

Asset rules

Use the full logo on light backgrounds, the flower mark for icons and decorative moments, the coloured face for story content, the outline face as a low-opacity watermark, and the tile pattern below 15% visual opacity.

Accessibility rules

Do not use green or yellow as small text on white. Use black text on yellow/green; use white text on red/black. Every interactive control requires a visible keyboard focus state.

Our story

From a Jamaican garden to tables around the world.

Flavour with roots

Long before we had a brand, we had Izelena.

Miss Izelena lived in the farming district of Aboukir, St. Ann, Jamaica and was an avid cultivator of Scotch Bonnet pepper. She loved the pepper - flavourful, fiery and full of Jamaican spirit - and she loved feeding people even more.

Today the family carries her name forward through a range rooted in the flavour she taught them to share.

AboukirFamily roots and Scotch Bonnet cultivation in St. Ann.
LegacyRecipes and a love of feeding people passed through the family.
IzelenaSmall-batch condiments designed to put Caribbean flavour at the centre of the global food scene.

06 / Page-by-page build specification

Functional and content requirements.

Required sections

  1. Announcement strip.
  2. Header with Shop primary CTA and cart.
  3. Product-led hero with two CTAs.
  4. Featured product grid.
  5. Scotchimeter heat selector.
  6. Story preview using face illustration.
  7. Recipe/use inspiration.
  8. Wholesale CTA.
  9. Email/social module.
  10. Complete footer.

Acceptance criteria

  • Primary shop CTA is visible without scrolling on mobile and desktop.
  • Hero has one H1 and meaningful image alt treatment.
  • Featured products are loaded from WooCommerce.
  • Heat selector links to filtered products only after heat data is approved.
  • No contact form duplication on the homepage unless analytics proves it necessary.

Shop archive

  • Filters: heat, category, size/use and availability.
  • Sort: featured, price, newest.
  • Cards: product name, tagline, image, starting price, status and quick CTA.
  • Filters must be keyboard accessible and preserve URL query state.

Product detail

  • Gallery, name, tagline, description and Scotchimeter level.
  • Variant selector for size/packaging.
  • Price, stock, quantity and Add to Cart.
  • How to use, ingredients, allergens, nutrition and storage once supplied.
  • Shipping/returns summary, related products and structured data.

Story narrative

Use the catalogue story as the foundation: Miss Izelena, Aboukir, Scotch Bonnet cultivation, family legacy and feeding people. Add the current site's mother-daughter ownership and local-farmer sourcing only as approved copy.

Visual structure

Hero with face artwork, chronological story, values or process, sourcing photography, founder/family imagery if supplied, and a shop CTA. Avoid a generic corporate “mission/vision” wall of text.

Form fields

Name, email, phone, enquiry type, order number when applicable, message, privacy consent and spam protection. Route wholesale, support and media enquiries to configurable recipients.

Contact information

Show address, Jamaica and USA numbers, email, business hours if supplied, social profiles and optional map. Verify every number and social URL before launch.

Why this page matters

The catalogue contains minimum order quantities, sachets and gallon sizes, indicating a clear food-service/wholesale use case. Keep wholesale separate from normal retail checkout unless the client confirms direct case purchasing.

Recommended flow

Benefits, product formats, territories served, minimums, downloadable catalogue, enquiry form, account approval, and optional wholesale role pricing in phase two.

Commerce policies

Shipping and delivery, returns/refunds, damaged goods, cancellations, privacy, terms of sale, payment terms, wholesale terms and cookie notice.

Do not invent

Policy content must come from the client and legal/compliance review. The implementation agent may create templates and placeholders but must not decide business policy.

Retail model

Sell individual jars/bottles online, with optional local pickup and shipping. Hide case MOQ from retail customers or show it only as a wholesale link.

Wholesale model

Require approved accounts, case quantities, role-based pricing and invoice/payment terms. This is phase two unless the client already has confirmed workflows.

Hybrid launch

Recommended: launch retail checkout for approved SKUs, while wholesale begins as a qualified enquiry flow using the downloadable catalogue.

Required product data before live checkout

Commercial

Confirmed price basis, retail/wholesale prices, taxes, stock, launch status, discounts and minimum quantities.

Fulfilment

Weight, dimensions, shipping eligibility, pickup rules, delivery zones and lead times.

Food information

Ingredients, allergens, nutrition, shelf life, storage, country of origin and regulatory label copy.

Merchandising

Final product photos, heat level, category, use cases, SEO copy and related products.

08 / Payment strategy

Use local acquiring first, global wallet second.

1. Powertranz

Role: primary card gateway for Jamaica/Caribbean merchant acquiring.
Implementation: preferably hosted or tokenized checkout to reduce PCI scope.
Dependency: client merchant account and bank-issued credentials.

2. PayPal

Role: PayPal wallet and potentially eligible card experiences for local and international customers.
Implementation: official WooCommerce PayPal Payments extension.
Dependency: verified Jamaican PayPal Business account.

3. Stripe

Role: future/conditional only.
Constraint: Jamaica is not currently listed as a supported Stripe merchant country for direct payment acceptance.
Rule: keep disabled unless eligibility is proven.

Naming update: “Atlantic Commerce” should be treated as First Atlantic Commerce (FAC), now Powertranz. Confirm the exact gateway/product and acquiring bank with the client before implementation.

Payment engineering requirements

  • Never trust totals supplied by the browser.
  • Create/validate the order server-side before gateway redirection.
  • Verify order ID, amount, currency and result on callback/webhook.
  • Make callbacks idempotent to prevent duplicate paid orders.
  • Store gateway transaction IDs and sanitized result codes.
  • Support test/sandbox and live credentials separately.
  • Test approved, declined, cancelled, timeout and duplicate callback cases.
  • Do not mark orders paid from a success-page redirect alone.

Simple enough to operate, strong enough to sell.

Theme

Custom WordPress block theme with theme.json tokens, reusable patterns and minimal JavaScript. Use the supplied assets and responsive, optimized derivatives.

Commerce

WooCommerce products and variations, HPOS orders, native cart/checkout, transactional email templates, coupons and configurable fulfilment settings.

Operations

Development, staging and production environments; daily backups; monitored uptime; security updates; least-privilege admin roles; documented rollback.

10 / Quality requirements

SEO, accessibility, security and performance.

SEO

Clean URLs, unique metadata, canonical URLs, XML sitemap, robots control, Product/Organization/LocalBusiness/Breadcrumb/FAQ/Recipe schema and Open Graph images.

Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA, keyboard navigation, skip link, semantic headings, labelled fields, meaningful alt text, error summaries, focus visibility and reduced-motion support.

Security

HTTPS, least privilege, strong admin authentication, sanitized inputs, rate limiting, secure secrets, safe file uploads, maintained plugins and tested backups.

Performance

Responsive WebP/AVIF derivatives, lazy loading below the fold, limited fonts, cache/CDN, minimal plugins and scripts, compressed CSS/JS and no full catalogue-page images in cards.

Analytics events

EventTriggerUseful properties
view_itemProduct detail viewedProduct, variant, price, heat level
add_to_cartVariation addedSKU, size, quantity, value
begin_checkoutCheckout startedCart value, currency, item count
purchaseVerified paid orderOrder ID, value, gateway, items
wholesale_leadWholesale form acceptedTerritory, channel, product interest
contact_submitContact form acceptedEnquiry type, no message content
11 / Delivery plan

Phased implementation and approval gates.

Phase 1

Discovery + content confirmation

Confirm commerce model, pricing basis, products, policies, gateway accounts, shipping zones, currencies, taxes, contact details and imagery.

Phase 2

Design approval

Review this prototype, choose page direction, approve colours/components, collect missing photography and finalize desktop/mobile designs.

Phase 3

Theme + content build

Set up environments, build theme/components, migrate content and configure product data without enabling live payments.

Phase 4

Commerce integration

Configure cart, checkout, shipping, tax, emails, Powertranz sandbox and PayPal sandbox; execute test orders.

Phase 5

QA + client acceptance

Responsive, accessibility, content, SEO, performance, security, payment and order-management testing. Train client admins.

Phase 6

Launch + stabilization

Backup existing site, deploy, validate DNS/SSL, submit sitemap, monitor orders/forms/errors and retain rollback capability.

Launch definition of done: all critical business data is approved; checkout has completed sandbox and live small-value testing; emails are received; orders reconcile in gateway and WooCommerce; policies are visible; backups and rollback are verified.
12 / GPT-5.6 Luna implementation handoff

Copy-ready agent brief.

This brief is intentionally strict so the build agent does not invent missing commerce data or create a visually attractive but operationally incomplete site.

You are the implementation agent for the Izelena Foods website redesign.

PRIMARY DELIVERY
Build a production-ready WordPress + WooCommerce website using a custom block theme. Do not build a brochure-only site. The design must match the embedded prototype and use the supplied Izelena assets. Use WooCommerce as the source of truth for products, variants, prices, inventory, cart, checkout and orders.

NON-NEGOTIABLE RULES
1. Do not invent ingredients, allergens, nutritional facts, shipping fees, tax rates, stock quantities, heat ratings or delivery times.
2. Mark unresolved business data as pending in staging; do not silently publish assumptions.
3. Do not hard-code products into templates. Seed/import them into WooCommerce and render from WooCommerce product data.
4. Do not collect or store card numbers. Use hosted/tokenized checkout supplied by the selected payment gateway.
5. Build and test Powertranz (formerly First Atlantic Commerce/FAC) and PayPal as separate payment methods. Stripe must remain disabled unless the client provides an eligible Stripe merchant account.
6. Use JMD as the initial display currency. Any USD checkout or currency conversion must be explicitly approved and tested against merchant settlement settings.
7. Preserve the brand story, Jamaican spelling/flavour language, and the phrase “Exotic Island Flavours for Every Season.”
8. Meet WCAG 2.2 AA for navigation, forms, contrast, focus states and keyboard use.
9. Optimize images and avoid loading full-resolution catalogue artwork on product-list pages.
10. Provide a staging URL, test credentials, deployment notes, backup instructions and rollback instructions.

BUILD ORDER
A. Establish theme tokens and asset pipeline.
B. Implement global header, announcement bar, footer, buttons, cards, form controls and responsive grid.
C. Build Home, Shop, Product Detail, Our Story, Wholesale and Contact templates.
D. Configure WooCommerce products and variations from the seed data; keep price-basis warning visible in admin until confirmed.
E. Configure shipping zones, taxes and payment gateways only after business rules are supplied.
F. Add transactional email templates, order statuses and contact routing.
G. Add Product, Organization, LocalBusiness, Breadcrumb and FAQ structured data.
H. Run accessibility, performance, responsive, checkout, webhook/callback and order-management tests.

QUALITY GATES
- No broken or generic image alt text.
- No German or non-English CAPTCHA/help text.
- Every form has server-side validation, spam protection, success/error states and privacy consent.
- Payment callbacks verify order ID, amount, currency and gateway status; processing is idempotent.
- Cart and checkout work on 320px mobile width through desktop.
- Product variants show correct price and stock state.
- Crushed Pepper Sauce remains coming soon until the client confirms launch and supplies final product imagery.
- Lighthouse targets: Performance >= 85 mobile, Accessibility >= 95, Best Practices >= 95, SEO >= 95 on key marketing pages.
13 / Client decisions required

Resolve these before enabling live checkout.

Products + pricing

  • Are catalogue prices per unit or per case?
  • Are they retail, wholesale or both?
  • Which sizes are available online?
  • Is Crushed Pepper Sauce launching now?
  • What are the assigned heat levels?

Fulfilment

  • Local pickup?
  • Kingston delivery?
  • Islandwide courier?
  • International shipping?
  • Rates, zones, lead times and free-shipping threshold?

Payments + currency

  • Existing Powertranz/FAC merchant account?
  • Acquiring bank and supported currencies?
  • Verified PayPal Business account?
  • JMD only or JMD + USD?
  • Authorization/capture or immediate sale?

Food compliance

  • Ingredients and allergens
  • Nutritional panels
  • Shelf life and storage
  • Regulatory statements
  • Batch/expiry information shown online?

Business content

  • Founder names and approved biography
  • Business hours
  • Verified phone/social URLs
  • Wholesale territories
  • Recipes and serving photography

Operations

  • Who receives orders and enquiries?
  • Who updates inventory?
  • Refund authority and process?
  • Hosting and maintenance owner?
  • Analytics and marketing consent choices?
